title: Interval averaging preserves the Lipschitz constant
statement:
Let $\eta>0$ and define the interval average of $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by
\[
S_\eta\psi(x)=\frac1\eta\int_0^\eta\psi(x+t)\,dt.
\]
If $\psi$ is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$, then $S_\eta\psi$ is also $c$-Lipschitz.
hypotheses_covered: A function $\psi:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ that is $c$-Lipschitz for some $c\ge0$
replaced: For $\eta>0$ and a real function $\psi$, write $S_\eta\psi(x)=\eta^{-1}\int_0^\eta\psi(x+t)\,dt$. If $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $c$-Lipschitz with $c\ge0$, then $S_\eta\psi$ is also $c$-Lipschitz.
